catalog.title: Blizzard just changed Alterac Valley in WoW: Forever. Pikaboo on AV players
catalog.description:
Take the towers first, or still rush the General? 👇

On 25 Nov Blizzard said WoW: Forever players kept finishing Alterac Valley without capturing the objectives, just rushing the enemy General. The changes: Honor and reputation for killing the General are significantly reduced; towers, graveyards and mines give more reputation (and slightly more honor). Generals and Warmasters/Marshals now start with a 4-stack buff (20 min) and every objective taken removes one stack. AV's enemy NPCs were easier than intended, so they now have more damage and health. Blizzard's goal: about the same honor, more reputation per match.

In September 2005, World of Warcraft's new Zul'Gurub raid gave its boss, Hakkar, a contagious spell called Corrupted Blood, and a bug let hunter and warlock pets carry it out of the dungeon and into the capital cities. Shopkeepers and guards caught it but didn't die, so they kept infecting everyone who walked past, and the BBC reported deaths thought to be in the thousands. Players fled, healers rushed in, and some spread it on purpose. Blizzard's quick fixes didn't hold, it restarted its servers about a week in, and the real fix, a patch that made pets immune, took nearly a month. Blizzard called it just a bug. Epidemiologists wrote it up in 2007, in Epidemiology and The Lancet Infectious Diseases.

catalog.title: World Buffs Do Nothing Inside Raids in WoW Forever
catalog.description:
World buffs like Warchief's Blessing do nothing inside any raid in WoW Forever. Out in the world, Warchief's Blessing gives three hundred health and fifteen percent haste. But the buff on your character says no effect while in a raid instance.

The buff text in WoW Forever (read November 20): Warchief's Blessing and Might of Stormwind, "Increases hitpoints by 300. 15% haste to all spells and attacks. 10 mana regen every 5 seconds. No effect while in a raid instance." The line shows on the buff on your character, not on the spell's own tooltip.
The same last line, "No effect while in a raid instance.", is on Songflower Serenade (5% crit and 15 to all attributes), the three Dire Maul buffs (Fengus' Ferocity, Mol'dar's Moxie, Slip'kik's Savvy)

catalog.description:
The Alcaz Operative Insignia is a hidden toy in WoW Forever: disguise yourself as a Defias operative from Alcaz Island for 10 minutes, 30 minute cooldown. In Alcaz Prison, skip the first boss, The Questioner. At the end, the prisoner Mason Connery gives The Man in the Iron Chains: kill the Questioner for his key. Bring it back for More Valuable Than Gold and Mason's Note, which points to Westfall. Upstairs in the Moonbrook inn, check the floorboards for a Document Box and turn it in (State Secrets) to Renzik in Stormwind, Nazgrel in Orgrimmar or Rix Xizzix in Booty Bay for a Fractured Insignia. Six make the toy; it is one per character, but the pieces can be traded.
